headline: US-Iran conflict escalates into a 7th day of strikes, dragging oil to $82 and rattling global markets — your portfolio felt it across the board today.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: Biggest mover in today's session, down 5%. The AI ETF was hit by a double whammy: broad tech selling on the ASX following last night's NASDAQ drop, and specific headwinds from Google delaying its Gemini 3.5 Pro model — a key holding in the fund. Market sentiment on AI names has softened this week.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE closed down 3.1% today — the worst performer among the Vanguard ETFs. Emerging markets got caught in the crossfire of rising oil prices (bad for oil-importing EM economies), a broadly risk-off mood driven by the US-Iran conflict, and continued uncertainty around Chinese economic growth.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS dropped 3.1% at today's close. Lithium sentiment remains under pressure — US major Albemarle is seeing earnings downgrades as lithium prices stay weak. Despite positive long-term EV demand stories doing the rounds, the near-term market is still sceptical on when lithium prices actually recover.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: GOOG fell 2.2% in last night's US session. The market is anxious ahead of Alphabet's upcoming earnings, and news that Gemini 3.5 Pro — announced at Google I/O — has been delayed by several months is hurting sentiment. Investors are worried Google is falling behind OpenAI in the AI race.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: MSFT slipped 1.8% last night. Analysts have been trimming price targets ahead of Microsoft's Q4 earnings report. The broader NASDAQ was down 1.4% on risk-off sentiment tied to the US-Iran conflict and rising oil prices, which dragged most tech names lower.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS dipped 1.1% today, tracking the weakness in US equities from last night's session. The S&P 500 fell 1% last night as rising oil and Middle East tensions spooked investors. Nothing structurally wrong here — this ETF is a very long-term hold and day-to-day moves like this are just noise.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: TTWO fell 1.2% last night in line with general NASDAQ softness. On the positive side, Take-Two's CEO reconfirmed GTA 6's planned release date this week and highlighted strong GTA Online sales — so the underlying business story remains intact. The dip looks like general market drag, not company-specific bad news.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG eased 0.9% today — a mild dip for a diversified fund that holds global and Aussie shares. The broad market softness driven by oil prices and geopolitical risk nudged it lower, but as a diversified multi-asset ETF this kind of daily move is completely normal. Sit tight.

watch_today.title: GOOG earnings incoming — big move likely
watch_today.detail: Alphabet reports earnings very soon (US time). Options markets are pricing in a significant move either way. GOOG has already dropped 2.2% last night as investors de-risk ahead of the print. You're sitting on a 12.6% gain on this position — nothing to do right now, but watch the result closely. Hold for the long term regardless of a one-quarter beat or miss.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — biggest daily drop in your portfolio
watch_today.detail: GXAI fell 5% today and is now down nearly 20% from what you paid. The catalyst is a mix of broad AI sector selling and Google's Gemini 3.5 Pro delay spooking AI sentiment. The long-term case for AI infrastructure growth is still intact — this is a lumpy, high-volatility ETF by nature. No structural reason to sell, but be prepared for continued volatility while the AI hype cycle finds its floor.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — lithium pain continues
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals is down 3.1% today and now sitting 35.8% below your cost price. The lithium market is still soft — Albemarle (a US lithium giant) is seeing earnings downgrades, and near-term pricing hasn't recovered. The long-term EV demand story is real, but the timing of a lithium price recovery remains uncertain. Unless your thesis has fundamentally changed, this is a hold — selling now locks in the loss at the worst point.

watch_today.title: Oil spiking on US-Iran conflict — watch your ETFs
watch_today.detail: Crude oil (WTI) surged 4.5% last night to $82.49/barrel as US-Iran strikes enter a 7th consecutive day. Higher oil is a headwind for global growth and especially for emerging markets (VGE holds many oil-importing countries). Keep an eye on how this conflict develops — a further escalation could weigh on VGE and VTS in coming sessions.

watch_today.title: VGE.AX — EM under pressure but long-term case intact
watch_today.detail: VGE dropped 3.1% today — the sharpest fall among your Vanguard ETFs. The combination of rising oil prices, US-Iran tensions and a slightly weaker AUD is hurting emerging market sentiment. You're down 3.8% overall on this position. Nothing broken in the long-term diversification story — emerging markets are a long game.

watch_today.title: MSFT earnings also approaching
watch_today.detail: Microsoft reports Q4 earnings soon. Analysts have been trimming price targets and the stock is down 11% from your entry price. The Azure cloud and Copilot AI story is still the long-term driver here — a weak quarter doesn't change that. Hold through earnings; only reassess if guidance is significantly cut.

world.summary: The biggest story of the day is the escalating US-Iran military conflict, now in its 7th straight day of strikes. Meanwhile, Trump is using the full machinery of the US government to push claims about Chinese election interference, and the FIFA World Cup continues to dominate the cultural conversation.

stories.title: US-Iran conflict enters 7th day — airports, bridges and water plants hit
stories.why_it_matters: US forces have now conducted seven consecutive days of strikes against Iran, hitting airports, bridges and water treatment infrastructure. Iran claims civilian sites were targeted; the US denies this. US forces also boarded an Iranian ship amid a ports blockade. Oil spiked 4.5% last night to $82.49/barrel in response — higher energy costs flow through to petrol prices and inflation globally. The WSJ is reporting both sides are 'creeping toward a wider war,' which would be a major destabilising event for global markets.

stories.title: Trump uses full government weight to push claims of Chinese election interference
stories.why_it_matters: President Trump delivered a major address claiming China interfered in US elections, stole voter data and committed widespread fraud in the 2020 and subsequent elections. He's using declassified intelligence files to back the claims. Fact-checkers from the BBC, Guardian and PBS have found the documents don't fully support the sweeping conclusions Trump drew. The move is seen as an attempt to delegitimise political opponents and reshape the historical narrative — with potentially significant implications for US-China relations and global trade tensions.

stories.title: FIFA World Cup crowds bring record business — but will it last?
stories.why_it_matters: The 2026 FIFA World Cup (hosted across the US, Canada and Mexico) has driven record-breaking foot traffic and spending in host cities like Seattle's Pioneer Square. Local businesses report revenues they've never seen before. The question now is whether that economic buzz can be sustained once the tournament wraps up, or whether it leaves a 'World Cup hangover' of inflated rents and quiet streets. Relevant context given Australia's ongoing conversations about hosting major sporting events.

stories.title: Global economic outlook — mid-year update flags risks
stories.why_it_matters: The mid-year global economic forecast update flags the US-Iran conflict and elevated oil prices as the key new downside risks since the January forecast. Inflation pressures that seemed to be easing could re-ignite if oil stays above $80/barrel. Slower global growth would weigh on trade-exposed economies like Australia. For investors, this mid-year update is a useful reminder that the 'soft landing' is still not guaranteed.

stories.title: China and Russia launch 30-nation AI body — US excluded
stories.why_it_matters: Xi Jinping has launched a new international AI alliance with Russia and 27 other nations — deliberately excluding the United States. The body aims to set global AI development and governance standards outside the US-led framework. It's a significant geopolitical move: whoever sets the rules for AI globally will have enormous influence over trade, technology and security for decades. This deepens the US-China tech rivalry and could affect companies like Alphabet and Microsoft that operate globally.

markets.summary: It was a rough night for US markets and a soft close on the ASX today. The NASDAQ dropped 1.4% and the S&P 500 fell 1% last night, driven by rising oil prices on the US-Iran conflict and nerves ahead of big tech earnings. The ASX 200 closed down 0.5% today. Gold ticked up as a safe haven, and oil is the standout mover — surging 4.5% to $82.49.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Closed down 0.5% today, dragged by tech and energy-exposed stocks.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Fell 1% last night — risk-off move as oil spiked and Middle East tensions escalated.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Down 1.4% last night, with big tech names selling off ahead of earnings season.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Surged 4.5% — US-Iran strikes entering a 7th day pushed oil to its highest level in months.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Nudged above $4,000 again as investors sought safe-haven assets amid geopolitical tension.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar slipped slightly, sitting just below 70 US cents.

politics.summary: The Albanese government has released its formal response to the national Islamophobia inquiry, acknowledging the problem is 'dangerously close to becoming normalised' — but drawing criticism for stopping short of the inquiry's key recommendation on terror laws.

stories.title: Government responds to Islamophobia inquiry — but won't change terror laws
stories.why_it_matters: The government's response to the landmark Islamophobia inquiry acknowledged anti-Muslim hate is 'dangerously close to becoming normalised' in Australia. However, ministers stopped short of the inquiry's headline recommendation: removing 'religious motivation' as a factor that can increase criminal penalties in terrorism laws — a provision critics say unfairly targets Muslim Australians. Civil liberties groups and Muslim community leaders are disappointed. The government says it will continue consulting on that specific recommendation, but hasn't committed to acting on it. It's a politically sensitive balance between national security policy and anti-discrimination commitments.

ai.summary: Two big AI stories dominating today: Google is under pressure after confirming a multi-month delay to its Gemini 3.5 Pro model, while China is making bold moves — launching both a new 30-nation AI governance body and the world's largest open-weight AI model.

stories.title: Google's Gemini 3.5 Pro is still MIA — delay sparks market concerns
stories.why_it_matters: Gemini 3.5 Pro was announced with fanfare at Google I/O earlier this year but still hasn't launched — and reports now say it's been pushed back by several months. This is a significant blow for Google's AI credibility. OpenAI and Anthropic have continued shipping models while Google has gone quiet. The delay is contributing to the sell-off in GOOG stock ahead of earnings and is a direct headwind for GXAI.AX, which holds Alphabet as a key position.

stories.title: China's Moonshot launches Kimi K3 — world's largest open AI model
stories.why_it_matters: Chinese AI startup Moonshot has released Kimi K3, described as the world's largest open-weight AI model (meaning anyone can download and run it). Open-weight models are significant because they let businesses and developers use cutting-edge AI without paying per-query fees to OpenAI or Google. Fortune describes it as 'Fable-level territory' — putting it in the conversation with the best Western models. It's another sign that China's AI sector is closing the gap with US rivals faster than many expected.

stories.title: OpenAI, Google and Anthropic in billion-dollar war to lock in startups
stories.why_it_matters: OpenAI, Google and Anthropic are now offering startups millions of dollars in free computing credits to lock them into their AI platforms early. It's a classic land-grab strategy: get developers building on your tools now so they stay forever. This massive spend on customer acquisition is why all three companies are burning cash despite enormous revenues. For investors, it signals the AI platform wars are intensifying — the winner will have enormous leverage over the next generation of software businesses.

stories.title: China and Russia form 30-nation AI governance body — US excluded
stories.why_it_matters: Xi Jinping formally launched a new World AI body this week, signed onto by China, Russia and 27 other nations — with the US pointedly absent. The alliance aims to coordinate AI development standards and regulation among member states, effectively creating a parallel AI governance framework to whatever the US and Europe put together. It's a geopolitical split that could affect how AI products are sold, regulated and used across different parts of the world — with major implications for global tech companies.

sport.summary: NRL Round 20 is well underway with some cracking results — the Raiders thumped the Rabbitohs 34-24, the Roosters beat the Storm 14-6, and the Sharks survived a late scare against the Knights 20-18. Warriors and Dragons are locked at 6-6 in the first half right now. On the AFL front, Fremantle are in scintillating form.

stories.title: Raiders down Rabbitohs 34-24, Roosters beat Storm 14-6 in Round 20
stories.why_it_matters: The Raiders were dominant in Canberra, beating the Rabbitohs 34-24 in a high-scoring Saturday afternoon clash at GIO Stadium. Earlier in the round, the Roosters were solid at home, shutting down Melbourne Storm 14-6 at Allianz Stadium on Friday night. The Broncos also snuck past the Panthers 14-12 on Thursday to open the round. Warriors vs Dragons is live right now, locked at 6-6 in the first half at Go Media Stadium.

stories.title: Sharks survive Ponga blunder to beat Knights 20-18
stories.why_it_matters: The Sharks held on to beat the Knights 20-18 in a thrilling finish at Ocean Protect Stadium on Friday night. Newcastle's Kalyn Ponga had a costly error late in the game that proved decisive. It was a nail-biter that went down to the wire — the kind of game that will feature heavily in the Round 20 highlights.

stories.title: AFL: Fremantle fire five goals in quick succession in big win
stories.why_it_matters: Fremantle put on a clinic this week, firing five goals in rapid succession in what commentators called 'a significant surge.' The Dockers are building a head of steam as the AFL finals race heats up. Zero Hanger also published an analysis today looking at the one major concern for every flag contender heading into the business end of the season — fitness and depth are the key themes.

stories.title: Geelong's controversial moment divides AFL world
stories.why_it_matters: A controversial moment in Geelong's latest win has split the AFL community, with commentators and fans saying they've 'never seen that' before. The incident hasn't been fully described in available article text, but it's generating significant social media debate and is likely to be a hot topic heading into the weekend's footy coverage.
